races.name: Racing To School Reaches 25 Years Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Minella Blizzard
runners_data.note: Unraced over hurdles with only a pull-up in Irish point-to-point, making him a complete unknown quantity despite well-connected breeding.
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a well-connected mare but was pulled up on his Irish point debut in April; the betting market may guide on this rules debut.

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with proven 2m hurdle form on good ground, showing consistency with recent win suggesting he's back to his best.
runners_data.spotlight: Well below the fairly useful form he showed in the autumn when beaten odds-on favourite in Plumpton maiden (2m, good) in April but made amends when winning tactical match race at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) last month; his profile is still not entirely convincing but he has strong claims here.

runners_data.name: Biggles
runners_data.note: Former high-class miler on Flat returning after long absence, with stamina questions over 2m hurdles but class advantage if fit.
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful on the Flat in his prime, with career highlight his 2023 Bunbury Cup success (7f; unraced beyond about 1m); absent since two below-par runs in spring 2024, though, and tricky to weigh up on stable/hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: White Riot
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with course and distance win but serious completion concerns having failed to finish in two of last three starts.
runners_data.spotlight: Won good-ground bumper by 8l in March 2025; rather disappointing when well-held third on hurdle debut in October and has failed to complete twice since but shaped with promise before weakening and falling at Southwell (2m, good) last month, after a break.

runners_data.name: Starshine Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping back up in trip after disappointing return runs, needing to prove hurdles form matches old Flat ability.
runners_data.comment: Entitled to improve for his comeback; claims going back up in trip having been dropped 2lb
runners_data.spotlight: Fair Flat racer who gained his win over 1m4f two years ago; back from long layoff with two underwhelming runs for new stable this spring but still has possibilities if he takes well to hurdling at the first attempt.

races.paceDynamic: White Riot will lead from the start with his confirmed front-running style, likely setting a steady tempo given the small field and lack of other pace pressers. The three hold-up horses (Loriko, Biggles, Starshine Legend) will settle behind with Minella Blizzard an unknown quantity but unlikely to press early. With no pressure on White Riot early, he can dictate terms and potentially kick clear before the finish, though his recent completion issues are a concern. This tactical setup strongly favours either the lone leader White Riot if he stays on his feet, or the proven hold-up performers who can pick up the pieces if he falters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: White Riot Stays Sound
scenarios.trigger: If White Riot completes the course without falling or pulling up
scenarios.body: His uncontested lead allows him to build an insurmountable advantage before the field can respond, with his 8-length bumper win proving his ability when everything goes right. The hold-up horses find too much ground to make up despite their superior ratings.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If White Riot's recent completion problems resurface or he's caught late
scenarios.body: Loriko and Biggles use their proven class advantage to overhaul a tiring leader, with both horses showing superior form figures and higher official ratings. Their patient tactics pay off as White Riot's stamina or jumping gives way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Minella Blizzard Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the lightly-raced debutant shows significant improvement from his Irish point
scenarios.body: His unknown ability level could be well above this grade, catching seasoned rivals off-guard with connections knowing more than the form suggests. The O'Brien stable's confidence in running him here despite his pull-up debut may signal hidden ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Starshine Legend Revival
scenarios.trigger: If the Murphy stable has found the key to unlocking his old Flat form over hurdles
scenarios.body: His return to a more suitable trip and good ground allows his class to shine through after disappointing recent efforts. The booking of Sean Bowen suggests connections expect significant improvement.

watchPoints.text: White Riot's jumping and willingness to complete given his recent fall and pull-up in last two hurdle attempts
Biggles' fitness levels after 747 days off the track and whether stamina holds out over this longer trip
Minella Blizzard's market moves as the only guide to his true ability on rules debut
Loriko's ability to close the gap if White Riot gets an uncontested lead given the lack of early pace
Starshine Legend's settling pattern as his Flat speed could see him race keener than ideal over hurdles

races.name: JAL Roofing Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Millena Agent
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up type with point-to-point stamina credentials, 61 days since last run could help or hinder fitness-wise
runners_data.spotlight: 2m4f Hexham maiden point winner last November (heavy), and best effort since when second in her members latest; some encouragement for staying trips on pedigree (family of Monger Lane), and won't mind any rain.

runners_data.name: Stavanger Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has shown promise despite being accident-prone, 12 days since last run suggests sharp and ready
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete in four hurdles runs for Daisy Hitchins; more required for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Accident prone during her time with Daisy Hitchins, albeit shaping with promise sometimes; failed to see out 2m6f when finally registering a completion on stable debut latest, however.

runners_data.name: Up The Hill
runners_data.note: Must settle much better than in bumpers, gains tongue-tie which should help temperament, 98 days off is a concern
runners_data.spotlight: Bred to appreciate a trip and hurdles, but must settle an awful lot better than on either bumper start last winter; gains tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Coumeenoole
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with clear class edge, recent 2-length defeat over 3m shows current form and stamina reserves
runners_data.comment: Value for plenty further than the near-3l verdict at Bangor latest (2m7f, good); up 9lb.
runners_data.spotlight: Miles clear with one other when beaten just over 1l in a Market Rasen 0-125 handicap latest (3m, good; RPR 118), and this novice contest isn't anywhere near as deep; yet to register form of that calibre with give underfoot, but possible he could get away with it here even if rain arrives.

runners_data.name: Presentandcorrect
runners_data.note: Natural leader who coped well with hurdles debut, strong finish last time suggests this trip will suit perfectly
runners_data.comment: Last of eight in Kelso bumper latest; more is needed now sent hurdling
runners_data.spotlight: 23l clear of Stavanger Rose when third at Cartmel on last month's hurdling debut (2m6f, good), beaten about 4l but quite strong in the finish; coped fine with cut in bumpers and argues a solid case.

runners_data.name: Executive Producer
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing improvement, 15-length fourth here latest with late weakening raises stamina doubts over this longer trip
runners_data.comment: Little show in a pair of bumpers and on hurdling debut in 2m4f Newcastle novice last month
runners_data.spotlight: Big uplift on previous hurdling efforts when 15l fourth over 2m4f here latest (good), though late weakening doesn't necessarily augur well for this step up in trip (didn't see out 3m in Irish points).

races.paceDynamic: Presentandcorrect will lead unchallenged from the start with Coumeenoole likely to track in second, creating a sustainable pace that won't stretch the field early. The moderate gallop will keep the small field bunched, with hold-up horses Stavanger Rose, Up The Hill and Executive Producer able to stay in touch throughout. This controlled tempo will set up a tactical finish where stamina and finishing kick matter more than early speed. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can produce late runs over the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Presentandcorrect sets a steady pace and the field stays compact
scenarios.body: The tactical nature allows closers to position perfectly and unleash finishing kicks when it matters. Stavanger Rose and Executive Producer can time their challenges to perfection from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front two pull clear
scenarios.trigger: If Presentandcorrect and Coumeenoole increase the tempo from halfway
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop stretches the field and favours those with natural pace and stamina reserves. Coumeenoole's class tells while Presentandcorrect stays honest throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained gallop throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly from early and stays strong
scenarios.body: The honest tempo exposes stamina limitations and favours those proven over staying trips. Millena Agent's point-to-point background becomes crucial in a test of genuine stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Sprint finish chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses converge in the final furlong after crawling pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where positioning and luck determine the outcome more than ability. Any horse getting a clear run can capitalise on the slow early fractions.

watchPoints.text: Presentandcorrect could go too fast early if pressured by Coumeenoole, destroying both their chances
Up The Hill's settling ability remains unproven and could ruin his chances if racing keenly again
Stavanger Rose has been accident-prone but could be overpriced if staying sound throughout
Executive Producer's late weakening last time suggests this trip extension may find him out
Millena Agent is a complete unknown quantity over hurdles but breeding suggests this trip will suit

races.name: Nourkrin Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tiger Orchid
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with solid recent form for current connections, though may struggle with tactical positioning from the back in a slowly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up all three starts for new stable towards end of last season; in the mix again
runners_data.spotlight: Four good efforts from as many starts for current connections, though once again wasn't quite able to convert a winning opportunity at Huntingdon latest (3m1f, good to firm); fair claims off an unchanged mark, and ought to cope with any rain.

runners_data.name: Secret Trix
runners_data.note: Class hold-up horse with good course record, but the lack of early pace could compromise his ability to get competitive from behind.
runners_data.comment: Creditable runs last twice, latest a third at Haydock on first run after wind op; chance
runners_data.spotlight: C&D record of 31133 includes a soft-ground win off 9lb higher almost two years ago and last month's perfectly serviceable staying-on 10l third in 0-145 company; faces an easier-looking task this afternoon.

runners_data.name: Belvedere Blast
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 158 days with strong June record, though the long absence and tactical disadvantage are concerning factors.
runners_data.comment: 2lb below August's winning mark (visored) but offered little since; visor still missing
runners_data.spotlight: Five out of seven hurdles wins have been recorded in the month of June; mark and trip fine, but although once a winner after 151 days out his record following an absence is a bit mixed overall.

runners_data.name: Noble Birth
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer lacking consistency and making only second start for new trainer, needs everything to fall right from poor tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Last seen tailed off in an Irish claiming hurdle; needs a revival and has topweight
runners_data.spotlight: Wanted for consistency towards the end of his time with Gavin Cromwell, and didn't see out 3m6f on April's stable debut; more in his favour here, but others more persuasive.

runners_data.name: Mammies Boy
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse with recent third place form, may benefit if traffic issues affect others but still faces the wrong race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ran his best race for current trainer when third at Exeter last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Despite again hanging left may have gone closer than a 2l third at Exeter latest (2m6f, good) but for whacking two out; stayers' trip asks a new question, but some appeal whilst still just below a winning mark.

runners_data.name: Breezethroughlife
runners_data.note: Prominent runner ideally positioned to track the lone leader, though recent form suggests stamina questions over this extended trip.
runners_data.spotlight: December's Doncaster second (3m, good to soft) suggested a sound future as a stayer, so it's disappointing he has not always seen out mostly shorter trips since, beaten 26l over almost 2m5f latest.

runners_data.name: Faded Fantasy
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with no pace opposition but faces 141-day absence and attempting to defy significant weight rise from previous wins.
runners_data.spotlight: Three good-ground wins at up to 3m2f during a profitable 2025, all off at least 9lb lower; yet to defy a break in excess of 45 days, so absence since January cannot rate a plus.

runners_data.name: Top Coeur
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer not convincing over distance recently, needs major pace collapse to get involved from his preferred back-of-field position.
runners_data.spotlight: Not seeing out his races at all convincingly this year, beaten 54l in a 2m4f 0-125 handicap here latest (2m4f, good); overlooked.

races.paceDynamic: Faded Fantasy will be the lone front-runner with no other natural pace setters in this field of predominantly hold-up performers. With six of eight runners preferring to come from behind, Faded Fantasy can control the gallop unchallenged through the early stages, likely setting a steady rhythm over this extended trip. The lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a tactical affair where the front-runner gets first run, while the large pack of hold-up horses will need to time their challenges perfectly from off the steady tempo. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent tactics, as the lack of early pace gives Faded Fantasy and Breezethroughlife significant positional advantages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Faded Fantasy maintains a controlled gallop and kicks clear approaching the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: The steady pace suits his stamina and tactical position, while hold-up horses struggle to close the gap having been outpaced tactically rather than through speed. His 141-day absence becomes less relevant when controlling his own destiny from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and allows superior class horses to showcase their finishing speed.
scenarios.body: Tiger Orchid and Secret Trix can overcome the tactical disadvantage through superior ratings and recent form, with the extended trip playing to their stamina strengths. The steady gallop actually helps these hold-up performers time their runs optimally.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Upset from Mid-Division
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner weakens dramatically and prominent tracker Breezethroughlife inherits the lead too early.
scenarios.body: Mammies Boy or Belvedere Blast capitalize on a collapse ahead while avoiding traffic problems that could affect the deeper hold-up horses. The combination of tactical position and fresh legs proves decisive over this staying trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Faded Fantasy stops quickly after his long absence and Breezethroughlife also fails to see out the trip.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a scramble where any hold-up horse with enough stamina can prevail, likely favouring those with proven form at the distance. Late momentum becomes crucial when early tactical advantages disappear.

watchPoints.text: Faded Fantasy may weaken quickly in the final half-mile if his 141-day layoff tells, potentially opening the door for a tactical scramble.
Breezethroughlife could inherit a winning position if tracking the leader closely but may not see out this extended 2m7½f trip based on recent efforts.
Secret Trix and Tiger Orchid face a tactical nightmare if the pace stays slow throughout, as they'll need significant luck in running from the rear.
Mammies Boy's tendency to hang left could prove costly if he needs to switch for a clear run in what may become a bunched finish.
The amateur jockey aboard Faded Fantasy may struggle with tactical decisions if challenged strongly in the closing stages after controlling the early pace.

races.name: JMI Planning 10 Years In Business Mares' Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Regal Renaissance
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with proven class advantage but stamina questions over this 3m trip despite recent Ludlow success.
runners_data.comment: Clear second at Stratford last time and appears capable of going one better
runners_data.spotlight: 2-13 over fences when trained by Henry Daly, the latter win gained at Ludlow (2m4f, good) last month; yet fully to convince stamina-wise over 3m but, having recently changed hands for £22,000, still has strong claims on this stable debut.

runners_data.name: I Am The Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to chasing after hurdles win but form dipped afterwards and previous chase efforts unconvincing.
runners_data.comment: Seemingly back in prime form in February but ended last season with two lesser efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to convince as a chaser in two attempts at last season; subsequently won over hurdles (2m3f, soft) but her form dipped afterwards; took step back in right direction when well-held second in four-runner hurdle last month (3m2f, good to firm) but needs another on this return to fences.

runners_data.name: That's Nice
runners_data.note: Will likely lead but disappointing since switching to chasing despite earlier promise over hurdles this season.
runners_data.comment: 6yo who is 0-5 over fences and was pulled up last time; others are more convincing
runners_data.spotlight: 2-3 as a novice hurdler during 2024-25 season but 0-5 and generally disappointing since switched to chasing in November; didn't run badly when third of four in higher-grade event here (2m4f, good) last month, though, and is still unexposed over this sort of trip.

runners_data.name: Queens Wish
runners_data.note: Prominent style with solid 3m form including course-and-distance type win at Southwell in November off today's mark.
runners_data.comment: Not disgraced in a better race at Warwick last time and could have a part to play
runners_data.spotlight: 1-10 for current stable over the last year, the win gained off today's mark at Southwell (3m, good to soft) in November; needs to bounce back from a disappointing effort over that C&D last month but ran quite well in a valuable series final two starts ago and is of interest here.

races.paceDynamic: That's Nice will likely lead from the front with minimal pressure in this small field, given her prominent style and the lack of other confirmed pace-setters. I Am The Moon and Queens Wish will settle in behind, with Regal Renaissance likely held up towards the rear given his hold-up style. The sustainable gallop will suit stamina-laden types who can pick up from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and late closers who can exploit the modest early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Finish
scenarios.trigger: If That's Nice sets an uncontested lead and maintains a steady rhythm throughout
scenarios.body: The even pace allows hold-up horses to travel comfortably before unleashing their finishing kick. Regal Renaissance's proven stamina and class advantage become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If That's Nice gets an easy lead and kicks clear approaching the final fence
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows her to conserve energy for a sustained drive home. Henderson's mare capitalizes on favorable tactics to overcome recent disappointing form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If I Am The Moon and Queens Wish press That's Nice from early and create stronger pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and favors horses with tactical speed over pure stamina. The prominent runners kick clear while Regal Renaissance struggles to close the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Collapse and Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If That's Nice fades badly in the final half-mile after setting the pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a staying test between the three followers, with Queens Wish's recent Southwell win proving key. Her trainer's 1/3 record suggests targeted preparation pays off.

watchPoints.text: That's Nice could steal this if allowed an uncontested lead given Henderson's 2/12 recent record suggests selective targeting
Regal Renaissance's 25-day break and stamina concerns over 3m could undermine his class advantage
I Am The Moon's chasing confidence remains fragile after previous poor efforts over fences last season
Queens Wish drops significantly in weight to 146lbs which could prove crucial in a tight finish
Small field of four means any early mistakes or jumping errors will be severely punished

races.name: Litholexal Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hillsin
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose recent poor form makes him vulnerable despite class advantage
runners_data.spotlight: The consistency of his summer 2024 campaign has long deserted him, the return to the mark of October's Exeter win (2m2f, good to firm) owed to three poor runs since; others convince more.

runners_data.name: The Best Way
runners_data.note: Last-gasp winner who needs strong pace to be effective from his hold-up style
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 8yo; won after layoff in February 2025; not seen since
runners_data.spotlight: Determined last-gasp Newcastle winner in February 2025 (2m1f, good to soft), and recent Hexham third on sole run since was much more promising than the 31l distance beaten might imply (rallied after late blunder); may be a case of whether this longer trip is within range now.

runners_data.name: Saxon Cross
runners_data.note: Consistent sort stepping up from novice company with solid recent form at the track
runners_data.comment: Second in a bumper last summer but well held on both hurdling starts this year
runners_data.spotlight: Last month's staying-on 5l fourth in a 2m novice here was given a boost by the third at Southwell two days ago; handy initial mark set against his bumper best; kept almost exclusively to good ground so far.

runners_data.name: Bells Of Ufford
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 70-day break which raises fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Late interference no help when a 5l fourth in this new headgear combination last time
runners_data.spotlight: Consolidated rather than improved upon previous best efforts during last season, despite the addition of cheekpieces; remains on a tempting mark, but significant rain wouldn't be welcomed.

runners_data.name: Pepite De Saphir
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trying tongue-tie for first time after disappointing debut for yard
runners_data.comment: Remote second at Newcastle last February; needs to hit the ground running for her new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Career already subject to two significant interruptions, and offered little in a debuted tongue-tie when starting out for current connections here last month (2m7f, good).

runners_data.name: Brionywells
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who showed career-best form last week and handles the trip well
runners_data.comment: The Uttoxeter fourth was better but she then disappointed at Sedgefield
runners_data.spotlight: Major personal best on last week's return from eight months out, staying on well late to take a 2m7f Worcester novice handicap (good); little to choose between her peak previous RPRs with or without cut, so possible she'll cope if the rain arrives; chance despite the penalty.

runners_data.name: The Padster
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing cheekpieces again after improved Hereford second
runners_data.comment: Had breathing surgery before remote Exeter fourth 25 days ago; cheekpieces are now tried
runners_data.spotlight: Back on track to an extent with last month's fast-ground Hereford 2m3f second in debuted cheekpieces (retained), albeit beaten 21l; ground slower than good would ask a new question.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer transformed by tongue-tie with two wins in past week
runners_data.comment: Hosed up back over hurdles yesterday and looks very well in under a penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Transformed by the tongue-tie, adding an admittedly poor 2m4f Southwell novice handicap hurdle two nights ago to last weekend's Worcester chase debut rout (2m, good); likely still well ahead of her mark, and just a case of whether a third race in a week or possibly softer ground find her out; also engaged 8:30 Warwick Wednesday.

runners_data.name: Bowling Shane
runners_data.note: Improving hold-up four-year-old whose better jumping inspired recent upturn
runners_data.spotlight: Better round of jumping inspired a major uplift on last month's handicap debut at Ffos Las (2m, good), shaping as if this longer trip might give him more chance of defying a still ungenerous-looking mark.

races.paceDynamic: Pepite De Saphir and Beorma will likely contest the early lead, with The Padster sitting prominently behind them. The pace should be honest rather than frantic given the trip and going conditions, with most of the field held up including Hillsin, The Best Way, Saxon Cross, Bells Of Ufford, Brionywells, and Bowling Shane. With limited early pace and a strong gallop likely to develop, this setup creates a tactical affair where positioning will be crucial. This race shape favours prominent racers and those with tactical speed who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will affect the large contingent of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady early and the field stays bunched into the home straight
scenarios.body: The large group of hold-up horses will struggle for racing room while those positioned handily can strike when gaps appear. Beorma and The Padster are best placed to exploit their forward positions when the race develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Pepite De Saphir and Beorma go fast from the start creating a genuine test
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will suit the proven stayers and those coming from behind will get their chance as the leaders tire. Brionywells' recent stamina-laden success and The Best Way's last-gasp Newcastle win become relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Pepite De Saphir finds improvement for the tongue-tie and gets an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The mare can dictate terms and prove hard to peg back with Beorma's recent form surge making him the main danger. The hold-up brigade will find the leaders have stolen too much ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Traffic Issues
scenarios.trigger: If the field gets badly bunched approaching the final flight with multiple horses needing gaps
scenarios.body: Several fancied runners will meet trouble in running while those with clear passages or racing luck will benefit disproportionately. The race becomes a lottery where positioning and jockey skill matter more than form.

watchPoints.text: Beorma has won twice in the past week and Harry Skelton's presence suggests strong confidence from the in-form Skelton yard
Traffic problems likely in home straight with six hold-up horses needing room in a nine-runner field
Pepite De Saphir debuts tongue-tie which has transformed Beorma for same trainer Rebecca Menzies
The Best Way and Bells Of Ufford both face fitness questions after breaks of 26 and 70 days respectively
Saxon Cross gets weight relief from claiming jockey Lee Edwards which could prove significant off his handy mark

races.name: Turf Services Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Immortal Fame
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who performs well here with some give underfoot, but 64 days off the track and needs to prove recent poor form was just due to unsuitable conditions.
runners_data.spotlight: 2m4f winner here over hurdles and fences with a little give underfoot, and possible excuses on both starts since his most recent success elsewhere (holding ground, pace battle); remains above any winning mark.

runners_data.name: Yes Indeed
runners_data.note: Proven course performer tracking prominently, but the addition of cheekpieces suggests connections felt he needed sharpening up after recent below-par efforts.
runners_data.comment: Won twice over fences at around this trip last spring; not so good since.
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable efforts on both previous course visits, including a close fourth in this in 2024; weighted to strike, but must prove that the effects of the cheekpieces aren't on the wane after a sub-par latest effort.

runners_data.name: Karnaval Point
runners_data.note: French import making only second British start for in-form Pipe yard, prominent style suits and 9lb rise for Worcester win looks fair for this step up in class.
runners_data.comment: 2m7f and more recently 2m2f chase winner in France; workable mark; market check advised.
runners_data.spotlight: Not hard pushed to score on last month's stable/British debut in a 2m4f Worcester handicap chase (good), for which a 9lb rise isn't harsh; French chase winner at up to 2m7f on slow ground, so appears to have an answer for most eventualities; player.

runners_data.name: Joltin N Jiving
runners_data.note: Switched to front-running last time with success and gets uncontested lead here, but 83 days since last run and jumping fences rather than hurdles adds uncertainty.
runners_data.spotlight: Resumed previous progression with last time's Doncaster handicap hurdle second (2m5f, good to soft) off 1lb lower; switched to front-running there, and would likely face competition for the lead if that strategy is persisted with today; retains tongue-tie for chasing debut.

runners_data.name: Tyson
runners_data.note: Hold-up stylist who looks well handicapped off bottom weight after recent hurdle wins, but this flat-bred 6-year-old faces a tactical disadvantage in small field.
runners_data.comment: Carries 7lb penalty for comfortable 2m4f win nine days ago; tries a new trip; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Newcastle and (latest) Huntingdon 2m4f class 5 hurdles winner either side of a stiffer task in a class 2; 10lb well in following the latter, but this Flat-bred didn't offer much in a moderate Sligo beginners' event on his sole previous chase start; 2nd at Warwick last night.

runners_data.name: Wheresmemoneygone
runners_data.note: Made all when winning at Taunton in February wearing cheekpieces for first time, prominent runner who handles this trip and going combination well.
runners_data.comment: Made all in a good time at Taunton, won readily and may have got off lightly with 7lb
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in debuted cheekpieces at Taunton in February (2m5f, good to soft); 7lb rise for posting that course record time was fair, and the subsequent Newbury defeat instead looked owed to the same sort of fight for the early lead which Joltin N Jiving might yet give him here.

races.paceDynamic: Joltin N Jiving will dictate from the front having switched to front-running tactics last time with success, while Yes Indeed, Karnaval Point, Wheresmemoneygone and Immortal Fame will track prominently in the early stages. With only one confirmed leader and five prominent runners, the pace is likely to be solid but not frantic early on, allowing the field to stay together through the first half. The relatively small field and sustainable early gallop will produce a tactical affair that comes alive in the final half-mile, strongly favouring prominent runners who can position close to the pace and kick when it matters rather than hold-up horses trying to weave through traffic.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays solid but controlled through halfway
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get ideal positioning to strike turning for home, with Karnaval Point, Yes Indeed and Wheresmemoneygone best placed to exploit their tactical advantages. Hold-up horse Tyson gets caught too far back when the race develops into a sprint from the final fence.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Joltin N Jiving gets an easy lead and kicks clear approaching the final fence
scenarios.body: The leader's stamina and front-running momentum proves decisive over this staying trip, with the prominent runners unable to reel him back in time. Karnaval Point and Wheresmemoneygone mount the strongest challenges but fall just short.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes overly strong and the prominent runners go too fast
scenarios.body: The patient tactics on Tyson pay dividends as the early leaders weaken in the final furlong, allowing the Skelton runner to sweep past tired horses. His class advantage from easier recent targets becomes telling when others have emptied their tanks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Joltin N Jiving goes too slow early and the field bunches entering the home straight
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace creates a messy sprint finish where positioning becomes crucial and any of the prominent runners can prevail. Traffic problems and jumping errors at the final fence decide the outcome more than pure ability.

watchPoints.text: Joltin N Jiving getting too easy a lead early - if uncontested through halfway he becomes very dangerous late on
Traffic problems in home straight given small field bunching - particularly watch Tyson getting blocked when making his move
Karnaval Point's jumping under pressure - still relatively inexperienced over British fences and this represents a significant step up in class
Yes Indeed's response to cheekpieces - first time headgear suggests trainer felt he needed extra motivation after recent disappointing efforts
Early market moves on Immortal Fame - any support would suggest the long absence isn't a concern to connections

races.name: Quinnbet Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lively Citizen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose 11-year-old legs showed signs of weakening at Aintree but the drop back to 2m could help
runners_data.spotlight: Long in the tooth and no longer the force of old but arguably ran better than bare form suggests when weakening fifth at Aintree (2m1f, good) three weeks ago, and this race is less competitive; could have a say.

runners_data.name: Zucayan
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs a strong pace to be effective and has won all three hurdle victories at Ludlow
runners_data.comment: Strong C&D record includes wins in this race in 2023 and 2025 (faller in 2024)
runners_data.spotlight: Gained all three hurdle wins at Ludlow; kept on for second behind progressive rival there (2m, good) last month, after a break, but may not be ideally suited by this switch to a left-handed track.

runners_data.name: Justus
runners_data.note: Prominent type carrying 8lbs less than last time out after showing return to form at Hexham off reduced mark
runners_data.comment: Latest run was step in right direction but he was generally very disappointing last term
runners_data.spotlight: Out of form last season but seemed to have turned a corner when second off much-reduced mark at Hexham (2m, good) 16 days ago; player if in similar mood again here.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner last month now 4lb higher but Sarah-Jayne Davies has excellent 1/7 strike rate
runners_data.comment: Juvenile winner for Sam England; good third to Spartan Times over C&D latest; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Came good for Sarah-Jayne Davies at third attempt, holding on well to make all over C&D (good) last month; 4lb higher now but won't mind if there's rain about; respected in current form.

runners_data.name: Ask A Sainte
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making handicap debut for in-form Olly Murphy/Sean Bowen combination, still unexposed at 6
runners_data.comment: Best run for David Brace when 5th in maiden hurdle; interesting on h'cap/stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 6yo who kept on from the rear for encouraging fourth behind Genbu over C&D (good) on last month's stable/handicap debut; probably still has a bigger run in him and features prominently in calculations.

runners_data.name: Calibos
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with only two hurdle starts under his belt, scope for improvement but hard to assess
runners_data.comment: Fair Flat racer who made satisfactory hurdle debut in March; considered each-way
runners_data.spotlight: Fair on the Flat at around 1m2f for the Kublers last year; safely held when making the frame on both hurdling starts for Jo Davis this year but improvement is possible on this handicap hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Clever Relation
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 462 days since last run and was well beaten in three novice hurdles previously
runners_data.spotlight: Won on the Flat for Hughie Morrison in 2024 but was soundly beaten at triple-digit odds in three novice hurdles for Sheila Lewis in 2024-25 season; makes stable/handicap hurdle debut after 462-day absence; could be considered only if lively in the betting.

races.paceDynamic: Lively Citizen will take them along from the front with Justus, Calibos and Clever Relation tracking close behind in the prominent positions. The early pace should be sustainable rather than fierce given the lack of confirmed pace pressers, allowing the leaders to dictate terms through the middle section. Zucayan, Ask A Sainte and Genbu will need to be wound up from the back but may find it difficult to make up ground if the pace isn't strong enough. This setup clearly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can travel well early and kick when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders aren't pressured and can dictate a steady gallop
scenarios.body: The prominent horses can conserve energy and outkick the hold-up brigade who won't get the strong pace they need to close effectively. Lively Citizen's experience and Justus's recent form improvement make them ideally positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If Ask A Sainte or Zucayan can generate enough momentum from the rear despite the modest pace
scenarios.body: The class and unexposed nature of Ask A Sainte or Zucayan's proven ability at the track allows them to overcome the tactical disadvantage. They'll need everything to fall right with the jumping and positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Course Winner Repeats
scenarios.trigger: If Genbu can overcome the 4lb rise and reproduce his front-running winning effort from last month
scenarios.body: The young horse's confidence from his recent C&D victory and Sarah-Jayne Davies' 1/7 record carries him through despite the weight rise. His making-all tactics could surprise if he goes forward early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders go too slowly and the race becomes a sprint from the last
scenarios.body: The fittest horses with the best recent form can capitalize on a messy, stop-start affair that doesn't suit anyone's natural style. Becomes a lottery where recent winners have the edge.

watchPoints.text: Lively Citizen may not handle the early pressure if Justus or Calibos decide to take him on for the lead
Zucayan and Ask A Sainte need to be positioned closer than usual if the pace becomes pedestrian
Genbu's jumping under pressure will be key if he tries to replicate his front-running winning tactics
Sean Bowen's tactics on Ask A Sainte crucial given the likely lack of pace to close into
Charlie Price taking the ride on Genbu suggests confidence from the Davies yard after recent success
